standard_prerequisites.name: Flat plus finitely presented is locally a summand
standard_prerequisites.use: E' is locally a direct summand of a finite free module.

core_obligations: After shrinking, choose the presentation α : E^• → E with cohomology isomorphisms in degrees ≥ a, replace E^• by σ_{≥a-1}E^•, and form the triangle E^• → E → C; from the vanishings, C ≅ K[2-a] with K = Ker(E^{a-1} → E^a) (proof lines 12575-12586).

Tensor with any F: tor amplitude of E forces the image of K ⊗ F → E^{a-1} ⊗ F to be the kernel of E^{a-1} ⊗ F → E^a ⊗ F, whence Tor_1^{O_X}(E',F) = 0 for E' = Coker(E^{a-1} → E^a); conclude E' is flat by the flat-tor-zero lemma (proof lines 12587-12598).

E' is locally a direct summand of a finite free module (flat plus finitely presented; Modules, Lemma flat-locally-finite-presentation), so locally the complex E' → E^{a+1} → … → E^b is quasi-isomorphic to E and E is perfect (proof lines 12599-12604).
proof_roadmap: Identify the cone of the truncated presentation.
Tor-vanish the cokernel and get flatness.
Exhibit the locally strictly perfect representative.
difficulty_reason: The proof truncates the presentation, identifies the cone with K[2-a], uses the tor amplitude to force Tor_1 of the cokernel to vanish, gets flatness and hence local summands of finite free, and exhibits the perfect representative.
